chunks: From him, from his father, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musalli, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: By Allah, you will be broken like glass, and indeed glass is restored and returns as it was. By Allah, you will be broken like earthenware, and indeed earthenware does not return as it was. By Allah, you will be distinguished; by Allah, you will be purified; by Allah, you will be sieved like chaff is sieved from wheat.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the glass and earthenware metaphor in the test of Shia during occultation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq employs the metaphor of glass and earthenware to illustrate the varying degrees of resilience among the Shia during the Great Occultation, noting that while some may be broken and restored, others face irreversible spiritual fragility. This narration, found in Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, emphasizes the process of *tamhish* (purification) and *ghurbalah* (sifting), where true believers are distinguished from the hypocrites like chaff from wheat. It serves as a theological reassurance that the trials of the occultation are not punitive but purgative, ensuring the community's ultimate fidelity.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 289 - It is narrated from Muhammad Himyari from his father from Ayyub bin Nuh from Abbas bin Aamir from Rabi bin Muhammad Musalli that he said:

Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) said to me: “By Allah, people will be broken up like glass, however glass can be joined together again. By Allah, people will be broken up like earthen pots; which if once broken cannot be joined again. By Allah, you people shall be crushed; by Allah, you shall be sieved, like wheat is sieved from the chaff.”
